name: Party_Member_MoveInventoryToBag
summary: Empties a party member's 24-slot inventory into the item bag: walks the used slots from the top down, unequips and recalculates the member for slots that are equipped, shifts the remaining ids left so the array stays compact, and adds every id to the bag at work+0x24ACC with ItemBag_AddItemCount(bag, id, 1).

The only caller is the SQCommand native 0x0015179C, i.e. a script command that clears a member's inventory. func_00191E3C (called in the equipped branch) is the equipped-first re-compaction: it saves the 24 ids and 6 equip slots, clears both, then rewrites the inventory in equip-slot order.

name: Sound_WaitForHandleOrTimeout
signature: u32 Sound_WaitForHandleOrTimeout(void* owner, float dt, u32* handle)
summary: Per-frame wait used by cutscenes and battle sequences to hold the script until a sound/voice handle has finished: accumulates dt into the float timer at owner+0x1234 and returns 1 (resetting the timer to 0.0f) once the timer reaches 1.0f or the handle reports stale, otherwise 0.
evidence: NEW: the disassembly settles it - `vldr s1,[r4,#0x234]; vadd.f32 s0,s1,s0; vstr s0,[r4,#0x234]; cmp r0,#0x3f800000; bge -> return 1`, else `Sound_GetPlayer(sp); ldr r1,[r6]` (the handle is *r1, a pointer) `bl Sound_Handle_IsStale; cmp r0,#0; beq -> return 0`. So it is a sound-handle wait with a 1-second cap, not a menu timer. The nine callers are all sequence/state machines that wait for a voice line: Ui_TalkWindow_RunMessageState, Battle_ActionSequence_UpdateTurn, Battle_ActorAction_ShowDamage, FieldParty_Ui_UpdateMemberSlot.

name: Field_GetActorAnimSpeedMultiplier
summary: Returns 3.0f in VFP s0 when allowTripleSpeed != 0 and 0x0062F110((work+8)->f_88) == 0, otherwise 1.0f. All callers feed s0 straight into 0x2D0E84(actor->f_B8+0xFC, s0) as the animation speed.

summary: Creates the five text rows (null_txt_l0) and the five 'next' icons (icon_next_0) of a paged text/memo window, builds the long-text layout for the body and selects the page indicator variant (2/3 rows) from the entry flags.

The owning class is therefore supported by two independent call sites, not just by the string literals.

name: maybe_Ui_EquipWindow_InitMemberTables

name: maybe_Ui_DebugMenu_CheckFrameSpike
summary: Detects a slow frame in the debug page: compares two frame counters and returns true when their delta is below 0x2E or at least 0x4C with debug flag bit 0x40 set; on a hit it clears the pending update and asks the view object for state 2.
evidence: NEW: the only caller maybe_Ui_DebugMenu_UpdateState uses the result to drive the page, and the 0x2E/0x4C thresholds plus the 0x40 flag bit are visible; 'frame spike' is a reading of those thresholds, not a named engine concept, so maybe_.

name: maybe_Model_SetAccessoryHandle
summary: Validates the tagged actor handle in self->f_1C->f_40 against the 0x007B80C0 handle table, lazily creates one 0x1C-byte vtable 0x00782950 record (guard 0x007BE2FC) and passes the handle plus the record's +0x54 list field to 0x001C7570. Nearby literals are 'meshAcc', 'Head' and 'R_Weapon'.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_WantsInstantText
summary: Returns 1 for message modes 0 and any non-2 mode; only in mode 2 does it build/look up the wide-layout table and return 0 when the layout entry's +0x46 byte is 1, i.e. when the text should be revealed immediately.

name: maybe_Ui_Panel_Notify
summary: Vtable trampoline: asks the UI core's text object whether it has content and, if so, lazily creates the 0x1C-byte singleton at 0x007F52B8 and calls 0x0019F4F0 on its second word. The frame argument arrives in r3 only, which is why Ghidra shows a void function.

summary: Refreshes a numeric counter/cost label: rebuilds the number object when the value class changes, otherwise formats the current value into the attached text object.

name: maybe_Actor_SetupEventActionList
summary: Event/action setup for a field actor: dispatches the model virtual +0x88, clears model+0x312 and then, when the model's action count is large, allocates and installs the emote, walk, climb and ladder action components through Container_SlotReplace.
evidence: NEW: the body is not the short 'end state chain' stub the old name described - it is a heavily damaged decompilation (unaff_r9, in_cr0/in_cr14, coprocessor_function) that installs a list of event actions (maybe_Actor_Action_Emote_Ctor, Field_ActorWalkTask_Ctor, Event_Climb_Constructor, Action_CtorBase). Only the component-install pattern is reliable, so the name is corrected and confidence kept at 0.3.

summary: Constructs a list-widget screen: installs vtable 0x76CF80, runs Ui_ListWidget_Ctor, initialises the list anchors and copies the owner's cached row data (0x84/0x44-byte blocks) into the new screen.

There is no direct bl/b call site (it is a vtable-only screen ctor), so the concrete screen feature is unknown - hence maybe_ at 0.49.
